semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: If integers a, b, r satisfy 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, and if for every positive integer d the floor inequality floor((r + b) / d) - floor((r + a) / d) >= floor(b / d) - floor(a / d) holds, then the finite product from i = a + 1 to b of (1 - q to the power r + i) divided by (1 - q to the power i) is a polynomial with integer coefficients, and every coefficient is at least 0.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
Because 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, the integers a, b, r+a, and r+b are all nonnegative, so every q-Pochhammer symbol appearing in the claimed identity is defined.

First consider the case a = b. By the definition of P_{a,b,r}(q), the product from i = a+1 to b is empty, so P_{a,b,r}(q) = 1. On the other hand,
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_a)
= 1.
So the identity holds when a = b.

Now assume a < b. We use the following elementary consequence of the definition of (q;q)_n: for any nonnegative integers m < n,
(q;q)_n = (q;q)_m \prod_{j=m+1}^n (1 - q^j).
Indeed, if m = 0 then this is just (q;q)_n = 1 \cdot \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j), using (q;q)_0 = 1; if m > 0, it follows by splitting the defining product for (q;q)_n after the factor j = m.

Apply this with m = r+a and n = r+b. Since a < b, we have r+a < r+b, so
(q;q)_{r+b} = (q;q)_{r+a} \prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j).
Apply it again with m = a and n = b:
(q;q)_b = (q;q)_a \prod_{j=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^j).

Since each factor 1 - q^j is a nonzero polynomial, these products are invertible in the rational function field Z(q). Therefore,
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= \frac{\prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j)}{\prod_{j=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^j)}.

Now reindex the numerator by writing j = r+i. As j runs from r+a+1 to r+b, the index i runs from a+1 to b. Hence
\prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j) = \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^{r+i}).
Substituting this gives
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= \frac{\prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^{r+i})}{\prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^i)}
= \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} \frac{1 - q^{r+i}}{1 - q^i}
= P_{a,b,r}(q),
where the last equality is exactly the definition of P_{a,b,r}(q).

Thus, in all cases,
P_{a,b,r}(q) = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
in the rational function field Z(q).
payload.role_in_assembly: Rewrites the original product into the balanced q-factorial ratio used by the later polynomiality, symmetry, and positivity lemmas.

payload.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate and define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when a = b. For each nonnegative integer n, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j), with (q;q)_0 := 1. Then one has the identity in the rational function field Z(q): P_{a,b,r}(q) = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b).

dependency_assessment.notes: Argument is purely definitional and algebraic; no external lemmas appear to be invoked.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof fully covers both cases a = b and a < b, with the empty product handled explicitly.
The expansions (q;q)_n = (q;q)_m * \prod_{j=m+1}^n (1-q^j) for m < n and the reindexing j = r + i are correctly applied.
The conclusion matches the semantic sketch exactly: an identity in the rational function field Z(q), not yet a positivity or polynomiality claim.

result_payload.reason: The proof establishes exactly the claimed q-Pochhammer identity. It correctly separates the empty-product case a = b, then for a < b expands (q;q)_{r+b} and (q;q)_b relative to (q;q)_{r+a} and (q;q)_a, cancels in the rational function field, reindexes the numerator product, and matches the definition of P_{a,b,r}(q). This aligns with the lemma sketch and its role as a product-to-factorial-ratio rewrite. No undeclared or forbidden dependencies are used.
